Subject: Post-demo: quick pricing units recap and a couple clarifying asks

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the deep dive, Alex & Maya. I wanted to capture a short recap on the billing/units questions we hit and one ask so our finance/pricing folks can give a concrete estimate:

1) Clarify what you told us in the call:
- Target monthly budget range: you indicated ~$4k–$10k/mo initially (confirm)
- Typical request shape: ~3–5 requests/min during peak, ~120k requests/month (confirm)
- Median prompt + response size: you said typical prompts ~1.5k characters and completions ~800 characters (confirm)

2) What we need to finalize pricing: two quick clarifications so we can produce a $/1M-token estimate and a 3-month cost projection:
- Please confirm whether the numbers above match your expectations (or paste your true monthly request volumes)
- Do you have a target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for (helps us recommend model/config)?

3) Token vs character vs requests: high-level notes so we’re aligned (we’ll confirm exact numbers after you confirm volumes):
- Redwood bills by tokens (subword tokens). Rough rule-of-thumb: ~4 characters ≈ 1 token for English plain text, but that varies with punctuation/formatting.
- Requests are not a flat billing dimension — you are billed for the tokens consumed by each request (prompt tokens + generated tokens). There is no separate per-request fee on hosted plans, only usage units.
- Prompt caching (optional): if you have many identical prefixes/prompts, our optional prefix caching can avoid reprocessing that prefix, which reduces billed prompt tokens for exact-match caches. It requires the prompt to be identical (or match configured canonicalization). We can turn this on for high-match workloads.

Next step: if you can reply with a quick confirmation of the three bullets in section (1) and a target $/1M tokens (or a monthly budget target), I’ll loop in Rishi to run two scenario estimates (conservative + optimistic) and send you a compact spreadsheet. If helpful, we can do a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to walk through numbers.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks for the ping. Quick answers and a suggested approach we can send to Alex: 

1) Tokenization guidance (structured JSON):
- JSON and long keys increase token count relative to average prose. For conservative planning we recommend using 1 token ≈ 3 characters for their workload (structured JSON with repeated keys/arrays). Optimistic (if they canonicalize keys/remove whitespace / use shorter keys) is ~1 token ≈ 4.5 characters.
- We can run a tokenization pass on their CSV examples to produce exact tokens-per-request; would prefer to do that before finalizing the quote.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens:
- If prefix caching is enabled and there is an exact match on the cached prefix, Redwood does not re-tokenize or re-execute that prefix; billed tokens for that request will only include the non-cached suffix tokens plus the generated tokens. In practice that reduces billed prompt tokens substantially for high-match workloads.
- Important caveat: caching is exact-match (or canonicalized exact-match) only. Partial matches do not get billed the same way — we can discuss canonicalization strategies to improve hit rate.

3) Back-of-envelope $/1M-token estimates (hosted API, list pricing baseline for conversation):
- Low-cost tier (quantized, good perf): $14 / 1M tokens (optimistic volume discounts available at commit)
- Higher-quality tier (larger model): $33 / 1M tokens

Given Alex's stated budget of $6k/mo pilot, at $14/1M tokens that’s ~428M tokens per month budget. With their median sizes that maps roughly to 75–140k requests/month depending on caching and the token/char ratio.

Next step I recommend: we run the tokenization on Alex’s CSV scenarios and return a short spreadsheet with three rows: conservative tokens, optimistic tokens, and cache-hit tokens — plus the $/month cost for the two model tiers above. Karthik — can you pull the model-tier perf numbers so we can include latency SLO notes?

—Rishi
